what: Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy, holds bitcoin as its main asset. It raises money by issuing shares and fixed-income securities and uses it to buy more bitcoin. It also still sells the enterprise analytics software the company was built on.
customers: Enterprise software customers for its analytics products; investors are the real audience for the bitcoin strategy.
money: enterprise analytics licences and cloud subscriptions
not revenue, but the main asset
bitcoin bought with proceeds from share and debt issuance
moat: None in the usual sense: the software is a small legacy business, and anyone can buy bitcoin. Its advantage is access to capital markets at scale.
risks: The share price is driven by the bitcoin price, with borrowed money amplifying both directions
Large reported losses come from writing down bitcoin when its price falls
Debt of about $7 billion must be serviced regardless of the bitcoin price
The software business is small and barely growing
opportunities: Bitcoin price rises flow through to the value of its holdings with leverage
It can issue shares above the value of the bitcoin per share, which adds bitcoin per share
Software revenue, while small, funds some operating costs
watch: Bitcoin per share, the amount of debt outstanding, and the premium to the value of its holdings.
